title: Floating column handle with live-measure overlay to improve resize confidence
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Users lack confidence when resizing columns in virtualized tables — immediate feedback is limited (pixel-only cursor) and interactions compete with virtualization reflow. This leads to accidental oversize/undersize and increased support requests when users try to match exported CSV widths or align columns across tables.

Proposal: Introduce a lightweight floating column handle that appears near the header on hover/focus which exposes a live-measure overlay. The overlay shows: current column width in pixels, suggested snap points (by column priority and content distribution), a small density preview icon (Compact / Default / Spacious), and an optional 'apply to all similar columns' toggle. The handle will be keyboard-accessible and provide ARIA announcements for live values. The floating handle should be implemented with minimal layout changes so it works with our virtualization/measurement cache and avoids costly reflows.

Goals: Improve UX for manual sizing, reduce resizing errors, provide discoverable density tuning during resize, and capture telemetry to inform future autotune suggestions.
acceptance_criteria: Floating handle appears on hover (mouse) and on header focus (keyboard) within 120ms without forcing a full table reflow.
Live overlay updates column width continuously during drag and after arrow-key increments; pixel value and suggested snap points are shown.
Keyboard interactions: Enter to enable resize mode, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight to adjust by 1px (Shift + Arrow for 10px), Esc to cancel and restore original width.
ARIA: Screen reader announces 'Resizing column {name}: {width}px' on start and 'Resized to {width}px' on commit; live region updates do not flood the SR.
Density preview toggles visually update a non-persistent preview of row density while retaining current KV cache and virtualization position.
Telemetry events emitted for: resize_start, resize_move (sampled), resize_snap_applied, resize_commit, resize_cancel with anonymized column priority and density preview choice.
No measurable regression in scroll performance or virtualization stability across existing heavy datasets (validated in perf harness).
Design spec and interactive prototype available in Figma; implementation PR links embedded in ticket.
design_notes:
Implementation should avoid DOM reflows inside the virtualized viewport. Strategy: render floating handle in a separate layer (fixed/absolute positioned relative to table viewport) and measure header geometry via getBoundingClientRect when a header enters hover/focus; use cached header metrics where possible to reduce calls. The overlay will be a lightweight element (no complex DOM children) with CSS transforms for position updates.

Accessibility: Use aria-live polite for non-intrusive updates and move focus to a small hidden control when entering keyboard resize mode to capture keystrokes. Ensure handle is reachable via Tab order and announce contextual hints (e.g., 'Press Enter to resize, Shift + Arrows for 10px steps').

Density preview: When user toggles density while resizing, we show a transient overlay mock of a single row height (not full re-render) to avoid virtualization churn. If user commits density change, emit a UX event and route to the density-setting flow (Console feature) — do not change persisted density automatically without explicit commit.
tradeoffs:
- Pros: improves perceived control, reduces accidental over-resize, surfaces density affordance during a related workflow.
- Cons: extra code surface (positioning layer, telemetry), potential slight visual complexity in crowded header spaces. We avoid adding persistent DOM elements to each header to limit memory/perf overhead.
- Alternate considered: inline persistent handles in each header cell (rejected due to virtualization memory and reflow costs).
comments: 2025-03-05 Aisha Patel: Created initial proposal after reviewing support tickets referencing 'column resize overshoot' and a quick guerilla test. Attached Figma wireframes and a short Loom recording of the pain point.

2025-03-10 Marco Ruiz: Implemented first prototype with absolute-layer handle. Early findings: measurement calls are the perf risk. Added a micro-cache for header rects and a 60ms debounce on pointermove when using mouse+.

2025-03-12 Elena Foster (Accessibility review): Reviewed keyboard flow. Suggested moving to aria-live polite and limiting announcements to start/commit to avoid verbosity. Also recommended explicit focus handling when entering resize mode.
2025-03-14 PR opened by ENG: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-ui/pull/1258 — includes demo harness and feature flag 'floating-handle-resize'.

2025-03-16 QA: Ran perf harness on large dataset (50k rows): no significant scroll jank; minor frame spikes during first handle show — mitigated by caching rects. Added follow-up ENG task to further reduce first-show cost.

2025-03-18 Marco Ruiz: Updated spec to include telemetry schema and sampling guidance (10% sample for resize_move). Marking AC item on telemetry as 'Ready'. Need PM approval to add telemetry to analytics plan.
